newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Berjaya Capital cuts stake in Dunham.
newsitem.headline: Berjaya Capital cuts stake in Dunham.

text.p: Berjaya Capital Bhd said it sold in the open market a 4.95 percent stake in Dunham-Bush (M) Bhd for 30.71 million ringgit, bringing its holding in the company to 1.23 percent.

In a statement sent to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange late on Tuesday, Berjaya Capital said the sale would result in an extraordinary gain of about 12.14 million ringgit, or a 2.1 cent improvement in its net tangible asset per share.

For the year ended April 30, 1996, Berjaya Capital, whose businesses include insurance, leasing and securities trading, reported a net profit of 97.71 million ringgit, or 17 cents, per share. Net tangible asset per share was 81 cents.
In the previous year, it posted net profit of 14.76 million or 21 cents a share.
Berjaya Capital said the sale, which was done from September 23 to October 21, involved 2.18 million shares of Dunham-Bush at an average price of 14.10 ringgit a share.

The sale of stock was to realise the capital gains from an increased market value of the shares and the cash proceeds would be used as additional working capital and to reduce its debt. No authorities approval is required for the sale.
The stock sale was done through Berjaya Capital units Berjaya General Insurance Sdn Bhd and Prime Credit Leasing Sdn Bhd.
Dunham-Bush is involved in air-conditioning and refrigeration equipment and related products.
